- Use coach demonstrations before live repetitions.
successIndicators: - Avoid late, high, low and rear contact.
- Select corral or smother actions when appropriate.
- Maintain pressure without unnecessary free kicks.
- Explain the reason for each decision.
matchApplication: Avoidable free kicks remove defensive pressure and give the opposition uncontested possession. Disciplined defenders influence play while recognising when contact is legal, unsafe or tactically unnecessary.

title: Match-Up Specific Tackle Planning
primarySkill: Adapting tackle strategy to different opponent types
objective: Develop individual tackle plans for opponents with different strengths, including speed, size, evasion, fend-off ability and preferred disposal side.
groundSize: Four contest lanes approximately 15 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
- Create four opponent profiles:
- Fast straight-line runner.
- Strong fend-off player.
- Agile sidestep player.
- Quick-disposal player.
- Assign one attacker to perform each profile realistically.
- Position one defender in each contest lane.
- Give defenders time to identify a pressure plan before each repetition.
- Rotate defenders through every opponent profile.
- Match players appropriately for size and physical maturity.
- All contact remains controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The defender reads the assigned opponent profile.
2. The defender states the intended pressure plan.
3. On the coach’s signal, the attacker enters the lane.
4. The fast runner attempts to use pace.
5. The fend-off player may use one controlled legal fend.
6. The agile player may use one or two direction changes.
7. The quick-disposal player attempts to release immediately.
8. The defender applies the planned approach, corral or tackle technique.
9. The defender receives one point for selecting an appropriate plan and one point for effective execution.
10. Players discuss whether the plan worked.
11. Rotate until every defender faces every profile.
coachingPoints: - Adjust the approach to the opponent’s main strength.
- Against speed, take an early pursuit angle and match pace.
- Against a fend-off, maintain distance until the arm is committed.
- Against agility, keep the feet active and protect dangerous space.
- Against quick disposal, close while the football is travelling.
- Avoid attempting the same tackle against every opponent.
- Maintain legal tackle height and head position.
- Revise the plan after each repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether defenders identify the opponent’s main threat.
- Whether the pressure plan matches the profile.
- Whether approach angles change appropriately.
- Whether defenders remain disciplined against fends and fakes.
- Whether quick-disposal players are pressured early.
- Whether players revise ineffective plans.
- Whether safety remains consistent across different match-ups.

commonErrors.error: Defender uses the same approach against every opponent.| Identify the specific threat and adjust distance, angle or timing.
commonErrors.correction: Player races directly at the fast opponent.| Take an interception angle and match speed.

commonErrors.error: Defender enters fend-off range too early.| Maintain the buffer until the fend arm commits.
commonErrors.correction: Player lunges at the agile opponent.| Corral and keep adjustment steps active.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts after the quick disposal.| Close while the football is travelling or as possession is established.
commonErrors.correction: Player changes technique so much that safety is lost.| Adapt tactics without abandoning legal head and body position.

progressions: - Hide the opponent profile until play begins.
- Allow attackers to combine two strengths.
- Add a support receiver.
- Use opponent-specific match footage before the drill.
- Continue into two-versus-two contests.
regressions: - Allow coach-guided planning before each repetition.
successIndicators: - Manage speed, fends, evasion and quick disposal.
matchApplication: Different opponents require different defensive approaches. Match-up planning helps players pressure an opponent’s weakness while reducing exposure to their preferred movement or disposal method.

title: Tackling and Pressure Match Rehearsal
primarySkill: Rehearsing complete tackling and pressure systems
objective: Rehearse all major individual and team-pressure behaviours in a structured match simulation before final chapter assessment.
groundSize: Full oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
- Divide players into two match-positioned teams.
- Play four scenario blocks:
- Stoppage and first-possession pressure.
- Defensive-50 exit and forward-half lock-in.
- Turnover and counter-pressure.
- Red-time full-ground press.
- Nominate player leaders for each line.
- Use normal AFL disposal and scoring rules.
- Match-like contact is permitted only for appropriately prepared players.
- Coaches observe without interrupting unless safety requires it.
- Record pressure KPIs during each block.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Block 1 begins from centre and boundary stoppages.
2. Teams are assessed on first-possession pressure and secondary stoppage response.
3. Block 2 begins with one team attempting to exit defensive 50.
4. The opposition applies a connected forward press.
5. Block 3 begins from an intercept, spill or coach-created turnover.
6. Both teams transition immediately into pressure or attack.
7. Block 4 begins with one team trailing late in the match.
8. The trailing team applies a full-ground press.
9. Coaches record tackles, forced disposals, receiver denial, recoveries and free-kick discipline.
10. Player leaders organise tactical adjustments.
11. Each block lasts five to eight minutes.
12. Complete a short player-led review between blocks.
coachingPoints: - Apply safe individual technique within team structure.
- The nearest balanced defender pressures the football.
- Supporting defenders protect dangerous space and receivers.
- Rotate pressure after every disposal.
- Release and recover after tackles.
- Protect vulnerable players at ground and aerial contests.
- React immediately to turnovers.
- Adapt pressure to scoreboard and tactical context.
- Avoid preventable free kicks.
- Use player leadership rather than constant coach instruction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether tackle technique remains safe at match speed.
- Whether pressure roles are clear.
- Whether receivers and dangerous space are protected.
- Whether stoppage exits are pressured.
- Whether forward-half pressure remains connected.
- Whether teams react immediately to turnovers.
- Whether red-time decisions reflect match context.
- Whether leaders organise adjustments.
- Whether free-kick discipline is maintained.
- Whether pressure KPIs reflect genuine influence.

commonErrors.error: Players chase individual tackles and lose team shape.| Reward connected pressure and receiver denial.
commonErrors.correction: Supporting defenders watch the ball carrier.| Protect the next disposal option.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers remain at the completed contest.| Release and recover into the next role.
commonErrors.correction: Pressure disappears after turnovers.| Identify the new ball carrier immediately.

commonErrors.error: Teams use the same pressure level in every scenario.| Adjust according to field position, score and time.
commonErrors.correction: Communication relies on coaches.| Require player leaders to organise each block.

commonErrors.error: Match-like contact becomes uncontrolled.| Stop play and return to controlled standards.
commonErrors.correction: Pressure statistics reward ineffective contact.| Count only actions that change possession, disposal or movement.

progressions: - Remove the breaks between scenario blocks.
- Allow captains to choose tactical adjustments.
- Increase match duration.
- Add opponent-specific patterns.
- Complete the rehearsal under controlled match fatigue.
regressions: - Use controlled contact rather than match-like tackling.
- Reduce player numbers and ground size.
- Allow coaches to organise each restart.
successIndicators: - Apply safe tackling at match speed.
- Adapt to tactical and scoreboard scenarios.
matchApplication: This rehearsal combines the chapter’s technical, tactical and decision-making content into one match environment. It prepares players for final assessment and identifies any remaining individual or team-pressure weaknesses.
relatedDrills: - TK-110 – Pressure Leadership and Tactical Assessment

title: Tackling and Pressure Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Final assessment of tackling and pressure capability
objective: Provide a complete chapter assessment of each player’s ability to execute safe tackles, make appropriate pressure decisions and contribute to coordinated team defence under match-like conditions.
groundSize: Full oval with six assessment zones and a final match-simulation area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
- Construct six assessment zones:
- Zone 1: Fundamental tackle technique.
- Zone 2: Moving and evasive ball carriers.
- Zone 3: Disposal, ground-ball and contest decisions.
- Zone 4: Two- and three-player pressure.
- Zone 5: Tactical team-pressure systems.
- Zone 6: Match-scenario pressure and leadership.
- Finish with a full-ground match simulation.
- Assign qualified coaches or trained observers to every zone.
- Match players appropriately for size, maturity and contact capacity.
- Use controlled contact for developing players and match-like contact only for prepared senior players.
- Apply the same scoring system at every zone.
- Record individual technical, tactical, physical and communication outcomes.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. At Zone 1, players complete stationary, side-on and moving tackle entries.
2. Observers assess approach, head position, legal contact height, wrapping, control and release.
3. At Zone 2, defenders face live evasion, changes of pace, rear-quarter pursuit and fend-off situations.
4. Observers assess balance, patience, recovery and tackle timing.
5. At Zone 3, players select between tackle, corral and smother around disposal, ground-ball and aerial-contest situations.
6. Observers assess decision quality, opponent protection and free-kick discipline.
7. At Zone 4, defenders complete two-versus-two and three-player pressure activities.
8. Observers assess role allocation, receiver denial, communication and tackle support.
9. At Zone 5, teams complete stoppage, corridor, boundary and forward-half pressure scenarios.
10. Observers assess structure, pressure rotation and tactical execution.
11. At Zone 6, players manage scoreboard, fatigue, chaos and opposition tactical adjustments.
12. Observers assess leadership, match awareness and adaptability.
13. Each behaviour receives:
- 3 points: Consistently demonstrated independently at match standard.
- 2 points: Consistently demonstrated under controlled conditions.
- 1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
- 0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
14. Any illegal, reckless or uncontrolled contact stops the repetition immediately.
15. Players complete a final match simulation in which chapter behaviours are observed without regular coach intervention.
16. Coaches produce an individual tackling-and-pressure development profile for every player.
coachingPoints: - Safety is the first and non-negotiable assessment standard.
- Contact must remain below the shoulders and above the knees.
- Head placement must remain beside or behind the opponent.
- No sling, lifting, rotation or unnecessary ground force is permitted.
- Players must decelerate before contact.
- Defenders should recognise when to tackle, corral, smother or delay.
- Vulnerable ground-ball and aerial-contest players must be protected.
- Tacklers must release promptly.
- Players must recover into the next defensive action.
- Team pressure requires one ball defender and connected support.
- Central and dangerous space should be protected.
- Communication and leadership must continue under fatigue.
- Match context should influence risk.
- Preventable free kicks reduce the assessment result.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Acceleration and deceleration into contact.
- Near-foot placement.
- Legal tackle height.
- Safe head position.
- Two-arm wrapping.
- Upright control and prompt release.
- Response to evasion, pace and fend-offs.
- Recovery after missed or broken tackles.
- Decision making around disposal.
- Protection of players over the football.
- Smother and corral selection.
- Receiver denial and defensive support.
- Pressure rotation after disposals.
- Corridor and boundary positioning.
- Stoppage and turnover reaction.
- Tactical adjustment.
- Communication and leadership.
- Technique under fatigue.
- Free-kick discipline.
- Transition after winning possession.

commonErrors.error: Player approaches contact without decelerating.| Restore the final short adjustment steps before reassessment.
commonErrors.correction: Head position moves in front of the ball carrier.| Return to side-on entry and reduce approach speed.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts high or below the knees.| Rebuild legal torso targeting under controlled conditions.
commonErrors.correction: Player reaches instead of completing a two-arm wrap.| Continue foot movement until close enough to secure the body.

commonErrors.error: Defender attempts tackles from unsafe rear positions.| Reach the hip line and move beside the opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Player tackles when corral or smother is required.| Reassess the possession and disposal cues before committing.

commonErrors.error: Tackler fails to release after a spill or whistle.| Make release behaviour part of every repetition.
commonErrors.correction: Player stops after the first pressure action.| Add recovery and next-action scoring.

commonErrors.error: Several defenders chase the ball carrier.| Allocate one pressure player and protect receivers with others.
commonErrors.correction: Team concedes central space while pressing.| Prioritise the corridor and greatest scoring threat.

commonErrors.error: Communication declines under fatigue.| Reduce work duration and require consistent role calls.
commonErrors.correction: Match urgency creates illegal contact.| Maintain technical standards regardless of score or time.

progressions: - Complete the assessment at full match intensity.
- Add opponent-specific tactical patterns.
- Use video review for individual tackle technique.
- Compare pressure KPIs with match data.
- Repeat selected zones under controlled fatigue.
- Allow player leaders to conduct the final review.
- Develop position-specific assessment standards.
- Reassess identified weaknesses after a targeted training block.
regressions: - Reduce contact from match-like to controlled.
- Use tackle bags before live opponents.
- Replace tackling with pressure touches where required.
- Reduce player numbers and field size.
- Return players to the relevant earlier chapter drills before reassessment.
successIndicators: - Use safe head and shoulder placement.
- Select tackle, corral, smother or delay appropriately.
- Adapt to tactical and match scenarios.
- Convert pressure into possession and controlled attack.
matchApplication: The final assessment determines whether players can transfer isolated tackling technique into safe, intelligent and coordinated match pressure. Successful players combine physical execution with decision making, communication, tactical awareness, discipline and repeat effort.
relatedDrills: - TK-060 – Pressure and Contest Block Assessment
- TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment
- TK-110 – Pressure Leadership and Tactical Assessment
- TK-119 – Tackling and Pressure Match Rehearsal
